newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian car industry welcomes tariff decision.
newsitem.headline: Australian car industry welcomes tariff decision.

text.p: The Australian car industry on Friday welcomed the government's decision to slow car tariff cuts, saying it would encourage new investment and lift exports.
Prime Minister John Howard announced on Thursday that car import tariffs would be frozen at 15 percent from 2000 and would be cut to 10 percent in January 2005.

"The government's policy gives the industry the green light to proceed with massive new investment and export plans that will see (the) automotive component industry reach its target of over A$3.0 billion in exports by 2005," the Federation of Automotive Products Manufacturers said in a statement.
Federation president John MacKenzie said Automotive Manufacturing Council estimates showed that exports of components could be worth as much as A$4.5 billion by 2005.
He said it was believed that as many as 5,000 new jobs would be created to meet this boost in output.

Car tariffs are due to fall to 15 percent by 2000 from 22.5 percent under plans already in place, and the Productivity Commission had urged further cuts to five percent by 2005. But unions, the Labour opposition and state governments warned that would cost thousands of jobs, adding to Australia's already high unemployment rate which is stuck above 8.5 percent.
